title: Monk Mode: how Iman Gadzhi clears distractions and builds a custom focus protocol
summary: Iman argues focus comes from starving distraction: block feeds on your computer, strip your phone, optimize your workspace, then run a time-boxed "monk mode" with a few non-negotiables plus your own variables. He favors a flexible protocol over rigid challenges like 75 Hard and starts beginners at 21 days.

principles.text: Focus is mostly starving distraction; remove clutter instead of adding productivity apps.
principles.quote: most people just have too much [ __ ] in their lives when they try to go online and learn a new productivity system you know they try to download a new app and what they do is they add even more clutter to their lives

principles.text: Use systems, not willpower: hard-block distracting sites during focused work.
principles.quote: it's not enough to say that you're not going to go on youtube or facebook etc you have to put systems in place to ensure it doesn't happen

principles.text: Keep the phone off and minimal in the morning; track screen time and treat lowering it as a challenge.
principles.quote: from my experience you lose 50 of your focus instantly right

principles.text: Use YouTube intentionally with a note-taking app open; most of it is procrastination disguised as learning.
principles.quote: if you do use youtube you want to use it in a very intentional way right so if you have a topic that you want to learn about look it up add it to your watch later

principles.text: Reward early profits with tools that make you more productive (desk, chair, computer, headphones) rather than status purchases.
principles.quote: when you're first making money spend it on making your life more pleasant and easier not buying gucci to impress people who you don't even care about

principles.text: Run monk mode with three non-negotiables plus two custom variables, starting with 21 days, because rigid protocols don't fit entrepreneurs.
principles.quote: i think 21 days for the first cycle in a case where you may not have the strongest discipline i think is a very very good idea to begin with
